chunks: My father narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Yaqoob from Musa ibn Harun who said:
I saw Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) looking at Harthamah in the city, and he said: 'It is as if I see him being taken to Harun, and his neck will be struck (beheaded).' And it was exactly as he said.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha (a title for Imam Ali al-Ridha, peace be upon him)
key_terms.ضُرِبَتْ عُنُقُهُ: His neck was struck (a phrase indicating beheading)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Ridha predict about Harthamah ibn A'ayan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the infallible Imam’s knowledge of the unseen (*‘ilm al-ghayb*) through a specific historical event involving Harthamah ibn A’ayan, a key figure in the Abbasid administration. The prediction of his beheading by Caliph Harun al-Rashid serves as a tangible sign of Imam Ali al-Rida’s divine leadership (*Imamah*), confirming his status as the designated successor. This event underscores the political tensions of the era and the Imam’s foresight regarding the fate of those who served the ruling caliphate.
